title: Body Systems
seo_title: Grade 6 Body Systems Worksheets: Cells, Tissues, Organs and How Systems Work Together
standard_text: Use argument supported by evidence for how the body is a system of interacting subsystems composed of groups of cells.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on body systems (NGSS MS-LS1-3): cells, tissues, organs and organ systems, the circulatory, respiratory, digestive and nervous systems, and how systems interact. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_sub: Cells form tissues, tissues form organs, and organs form systems. Systems like the heart and lungs interact to keep you alive.
body_html:
How to think about it

The body is organized in levels: cells → tissues → organs → organ systems → organism.

  • Circulatory system (heart, blood vessels, blood): moves blood that carries oxygen and nutrients to every cell.
  • Respiratory system (lungs, trachea (windpipe), diaphragm): takes in oxygen and gets rid of carbon dioxide.
  • Digestive system (stomach, small intestine, esophagus): breaks food down into nutrients the body can use.
  • Nervous system (brain, spinal cord, nerves): collects information and sends messages that control the body.
  • Muscular system (skeletal muscles, biceps, tendons): moves the body by pulling on bones.
  • Skeletal system (bones, skull, ribs): supports the body and protects organs.
  • Excretory system (kidneys, bladder, skin (sweat)): removes wastes from the body.

Systems work together. When you exercise, the nervous system signals the muscles, the lungs take in more oxygen, and the heart pumps faster to deliver it.

Example

Is the stomach a tissue, an organ or a system?

It is made of several tissues.

Answer: an organ

Example

Which systems work together when you run?

Muscles move.

Lungs and heart supply oxygen.

Answer: muscular, respiratory and circulatory

Common mistakes

  • Thinking each system works alone.
  • Mixing up the order of levels: a tissue is smaller than an organ.
  • Putting the heart in the respiratory system. It is in the circulatory system.

faq.q: What are the levels of organization in the body?
faq.a: Cells form tissues, tissues form organs, organs form organ systems, and organ systems make up the organism.

faq.q: How do the respiratory and circulatory systems work together?
faq.a: The lungs take in oxygen, and the heart pumps blood that carries the oxygen to every cell.

faq.q: What happens to body systems during exercise?
faq.a: The muscles work harder, the nervous system coordinates them, and the heart and lungs speed up to deliver more oxygen.
